question: Can measurement guidance through a Tweedie-denoised estimate keep unconditional diffusion inverse-problem trajectories aligned with the data manifold and improve reconstruction?

key_findings.claim: MCG backpropagates measurement error through the diffusion model's Tweedie posterior-mean estimate before applying exact data consistency.
key_findings.evidence: At each reverse step, the algorithm estimates clean x0 from noisy xi, differentiates ||W(y-H*x0_hat(xi))||^2 with respect to xi, adds this correction to the unconditional reverse update, and then projects the result onto the measurement-consistent affine set. It requires no inverse-task-specific retraining for linear H.

key_findings.claim: Under an exact score and a locally affine, uniformly distributed data-manifold model, the MCG direction is tangent at the denoised point.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 2 treats the Tweedie map as a local orthogonal projection onto M. Theorem 1 then writes the guidance gradient as -2 J_Q^T H^T W^T W(y-H*x0_hat), which lies in the tangent space. This shows tangency of a direction at Q_i(x_i), not posterior correctness for a curved empirical image manifold.

key_findings.claim: MCG substantially improves difficult inpainting across FFHQ and ImageNet when the diffusion score is held fixed.
key_findings.evidence: On FFHQ random 90-95% missing pixels, MCG reports FID 21.4 and LPIPS 0.186 versus RePaint 38.1/0.240, score-SDE 109.3/0.674, and DDRM 111.6/0.774. On ImageNet random masks it reports 34.8/0.308 versus RePaint 59.3/0.387 and score-SDE 143.5/0.758. It is also competitive with task-trained baselines across several masks.

key_findings.claim: The same guidance improves colorization and simulated sparse-view CT, including over supervised baselines on the reported metrics.
key_findings.evidence: For FFHQ/LSUN colorization, MCG reports SSIM 0.951/0.959 and LPIPS 0.146/0.160. For 18-view AAPM CT it reports 33.57 dB PSNR and 0.956 SSIM versus score-CT 29.85/0.897, cGAN 24.38/0.823, and FISTA-TV 21.57/0.791; 30-view MCG reaches 36.09/0.971.

key_findings.claim: Both manifold guidance and the final projection are necessary: guidance improves perceptual quality while projection restores exact measurements.
key_findings.evidence: On FFHQ box inpainting, projection alone gives LPIPS 0.138 with zero consistency MSE; clean-estimate MCG alone improves LPIPS to 0.124 but has MSE 10.7; their combination reaches 0.089 with zero MSE. Guidance on the noisy intermediate rather than the Tweedie estimate performs worse.

key_findings.claim: Quality comes with severe latency and dependence on the pretrained prior.
key_findings.evidence: MCG takes 81.59 seconds per inpainted image versus 38.68 for score-SDE, 2.117 for DDRM, and below one second for LaMa/AOT-GAN in the table; appendix implementation reports about 90 seconds for 1,000-NFE inpainting and 600 seconds for 4,000-NFE colorization/CT. Low-measurement regimes and ImageNet half masks can yield unrealistic symmetric hallucinations.

method.core_idea: Evaluate the likelihood at the diffusion denoiser's clean posterior-mean estimate so its Jacobian filters measurement guidance into directions supported by the learned image prior.
method.mechanism: Use Tweedie's formula Q_i(x_i)=(x_i+b_i^2 s_theta(x_i,i))/a_i to estimate x0. Backpropagate a weighted linear measurement residual through Q_i, add the scaled gradient to each stochastic reverse-diffusion step, and apply a problem-specific projection that exactly inserts observed components. Reuse an unconditional score model across inpainting masks, grayscale operators, and CT projections.
assumptions: The clean data occupy a low-dimensional manifold that is locally affine and approximately uniformly distributed in the theoretical neighborhood.
The score model is globally optimal enough that Tweedie's map behaves like an orthogonal projection near sampled points.
The known measurement operator is linear and supports the required projection/data-consistency calculation.
A perceptually plausible sample from the pretrained prior is an appropriate reconstruction when measurements are underdetermined.
The guidance scale can be tuned over a broad stable range without ground-truth leakage.
Image-quality metrics on synthetic corruption predict fidelity in real inverse problems.

techniques.role: Maps each noisy diffusion state to an empirical-Bayes estimate of the clean signal.
Backpropagates measurement mismatch through the denoiser to obtain prior-aligned guidance.
Restores exact consistency after the perceptual manifold correction.
Applies one pretrained score network to multiple linear corruptions without task-specific training.
Produces alternative plausible reconstructions for the same underdetermined measurement.
Stabilizes alpha across reverse steps by scaling with residual norm.

evaluations.setting: FFHQ and ImageNet 256x256 inpainting over box, random 90-95%-missing, extreme, and wide masks with shared pretrained scores.
evaluations.metric: FID-1k, LPIPS, visual quality, measurement MSE, NFE curves, and wall-clock time.
evaluations.result: MCG is best or near-best across most masks and dramatically improves random/extreme masks over projection-only diffusion baselines, at 81.59 seconds per example in the runtime table.
evaluations.baseline: Score-SDE, RePaint, DDRM, IAGAN, LaMa, AOT-GAN, ICT, and DSI.

evaluations.metric: SSIM and LPIPS over held-out images.
evaluations.result: MCG obtains 0.951/0.146 on FFHQ and 0.959/0.160 on LSUN, favorable to score-SDE, DDRM, cINN, and pix2pix.
evaluations.baseline: Score-SDE, DDRM, conditional invertible networks, and pix2pix.

evaluations.setting: Simulated 18- and 30-view parallel-beam CT on 421 held-out AAPM slices with a score trained on 3,839 images.
evaluations.result: MCG reaches 33.57/0.956 at 18 views and 36.09/0.971 at 30 views, leading all reported methods.
evaluations.baseline: Score-CT, SIN-4c-PRN, cGAN, FISTA-TV, and filtered backprojection.

limitations: The tangent theorem assumes an exact score and an exceptionally strong locally affine/uniform manifold; real image distributions are curved, multimodal, bounded, and nonuniform.
A uniform probability distribution on an unbounded affine subspace is improper; bounded uniform support introduces boundaries that complicate the claimed orthogonal-projection Jacobian.
The theorem proves a guidance direction is tangent at a Tweedie estimate, not that discrete approximate-score iterates remain on a real data manifold or sample the exact posterior.
MCG requires a backward pass through the score network at every step and is far slower than DDRM and task-specific feed-forward restoration.
Experiments largely use noiseless, known linear synthetic corruptions; real CT physics, noise, motion, and distribution shift are not evaluated.
Perceptual priors hallucinate unsupported symmetric structures at extreme masks and may create clinically unsafe details.
FID-1k uses only 1,000 samples and reconstruction metrics do not assess posterior calibration or coverage.
The method relies on prior training data and can reproduce its biases or malicious content.
failure_modes: An inaccurate score produces a misleading Tweedie Jacobian that steers measurement guidance toward prior artifacts.
Very sparse measurements leave many plausible modes and one stochastic reconstruction hallucinates an incorrect but high-scoring structure.
Guidance alpha is too large, causing exploding gradients and saturated reconstruction, or too small, collapsing to projection-only behavior.
A forward operator outside the training assumptions is nonlinear, noisy, or ill calibrated, so exact projection is unavailable or wrong.
A test image lies off the training distribution and the prior resists the true solution despite measurement evidence.
Thousands of score and backward evaluations make the solver operationally infeasible.
reusable_insights: Apply likelihood gradients through a denoised clean-state estimate rather than directly to a highly noisy diffusion state.
Separate perceptual prior guidance from hard measurement consistency; each fixes a distinct failure in underdetermined reconstruction.
Hold the score network fixed when comparing inverse samplers so gains are attributable to inference.
Report reconstruction quality jointly with consistency, latency, posterior diversity, and hallucination risk.
Stress-test extreme missingness and out-of-distribution operators because average image metrics hide prior-dominated failures.
Distinguish a geometric intuition under an ideal affine manifold from guarantees for realistic learned scores.
open_questions: Can posterior sampling guarantees be obtained for curved, nonuniform data manifolds and approximate learned scores?
How can Jacobian-vector guidance be approximated without a full backpropagation at every diffusion step?
Does MCG produce calibrated posterior samples or only high-quality point reconstructions?
How should uncertainty and hallucination be validated in real sparse-view CT with measurement/model mismatch?
Can adaptive guidance detect when the prior conflicts with data and defer rather than invent structure?
Which accelerated solvers preserve MCG's perceptual gains below 20 neural evaluations?

competitive_landscape.title: Denoising Diffusion Restoration Models
competitive_landscape.difference: DDRM performs conditional reverse diffusion in the measurement operator's SVD basis and can solve linear inverse problems in about 20 steps. MCG avoids an SVD-specific derivation and is stronger on severe masks, but its backpropagated 1,000-step guidance is much slower.

competitive_landscape.title: RePaint: Inpainting using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
competitive_landscape.difference: RePaint repeatedly jumps forward and backward while injecting known pixels to harmonize inpainting boundaries. MCG uses one tangent-inspired gradient plus projection per step, generalizes to other linear operators, and improves severe masks with less resampling but remains expensive.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems
competitive_landscape.difference: DPS generalizes the same Tweedie-through-likelihood gradient to noisy nonlinear operators and drops strict projection, interpreting it as approximate posterior guidance. It broadens MCG's applicability but retains costly backpropagation and an approximate likelihood score.

competitive_landscape.title: Zero-Shot Image Restoration Using Denoising Diffusion Null-Space Model
competitive_landscape.difference: DDNM analytically decomposes linear inverse reconstruction into range and null-space components and enforces consistency without task retraining. It offers a more explicit linear-algebra route than MCG's manifold narrative and develops noisy variants, while still depending on the diffusion prior.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Model Based Posterior Sampling for Noisy Linear Inverse Problems
competitive_landscape.difference: DMPS replaces backpropagated DPS-style likelihood guidance with a closed-form approximation for noisy linear problems and supports diffusion or flow priors. It directly addresses MCG's inference bottleneck, with narrower operator scope than DPS but substantially faster sampling.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a few-line manifold-constrained correction that makes general diffusion inverse solvers theoretically better aligned and empirically state of the art across inpainting, colorization, and CT.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the idealized tangency result; Tables 1-5 and ablations show large quality gains with a shared score and exact measurement consistency.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Backpropagating fidelity through the Tweedie clean estimate is an influential, reusable step that directly led to DPS. The 'manifold constraint' guarantee is much narrower than the empirical algorithm: its affine-uniform exact-score assumptions do not justify posterior correctness on images, and speed/hallucination remain major costs.

reviewer_notes: Read all 29 cached pages, including proofs, algorithms, experimental details, and failure examples. Competitors were checked from primary arXiv/OpenReview/PMLR records through 2025 on 2026-08-23. The theory audit separates tangent-vector membership under Assumption 1 from the stronger prose claim that approximate trajectories remain on a realistic data manifold.
